# Environmental mean IPM {#ipm_mean_env}
## Introduction

This analysis develops a mean integral projection model (IPM) for
*Eriogonum longifolium* using annual demographic observations from Archbold
Biological Station from 1990 to 2013. The model describes transitions among
active plants distributed continuously by size and a discrete dormant state.
Demographic processes include survival, growth, entry into dormancy,
reactivation from dormancy, flowering, flowering-scape production, and
recruitment.

The main objective is to incorporate fire while retaining its temporal position
relative to the annual demographic transition. Disturbance during the focal
transition from year $t$ to $t+1$ is termed **current disturbance**, whereas
disturbance during the preceding transition from $t-1$ to $t$ is termed
**previous disturbance**. These two disturbance variables are not assumed to
affect all vital rates in the same way. Instead, each vital rate is evaluated
using the disturbance timing that is biologically associated with that process.

Survival, growth, dormancy entry, and reactivation are evaluated with current
disturbance because they describe the fate of individuals during the transition
from $t$ to $t+1$. Flowering probability and the number of flowering scapes are
evaluated with previous disturbance because reproductive condition at census
$t$ may reflect disturbance experienced during the preceding annual interval.
Recruitment links flowering scapes at $t$ to recruits observed at $t+1$ and is
therefore evaluated with current disturbance.

For each size-dependent vital rate, alternative models ranging from an
intercept-only model through cubic size dependence are compared using AICc.
For each polynomial degree, models with and without the corresponding
disturbance effect are compared on the same set of observations. The
best-supported models are then combined into a single mean parameter set for
the IPM.

Because current and previous disturbance can occur in four combinations, four
demographic kernels are constructed:

1. no current or previous disturbance,
2. current disturbance only,
3. previous disturbance only, and
4. disturbance in both intervals.

These kernels describe fixed disturbance scenarios, but the historical fire
regime is represented separately. Observed transitions between previous and
current disturbance states are used to estimate
$P(D_t \mid D_{t-1})$. The four demographic kernels are then combined with
these transition probabilities in an environmental-history megamatrix. This
allows population structure and disturbance history to evolve jointly rather
than averaging the four disturbance-specific population growth rates.

Population growth is evaluated in two complementary ways. Asymptotic
population growth, $\lambda$, is calculated from the dominant eigenvalue of
each projection matrix. One-step projected growth is additionally calculated
by applying each kernel to the mean observed population structure. The
environmental-history projection begins with the observed population divided
between the two previous-disturbance states according to their observed
frequencies. These model-based growth rates are finally compared with observed
annual changes in population abundance.

### Survival
#### Data

```{r}
  filter(
    state == "active",
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_su_00 <- glm(
  survives ~ 1,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_0 <- glm(
  survives ~ disturbance,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_10 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_1 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + disturbance,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_20 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_2 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + disturbance,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_30 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mod_su_3 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3 + disturbance,
  data = df_su, family = binomial)

mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_00, mod_su_0, mod_su_10, mod_su_1,
  mod_su_20, mod_su_2, mod_su_30, mod_su_3)

mods_su_dAICc <- AICctab(
  mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- which.min(mods_su_dAICc)
} else {
  keep <- 2 * v_mod_set_su + c(1, 2)
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- keep[which.min(mods_su_dAICc[keep])]
}

v_mod_su_index <- floor((mod_su_index_bestfit - 1) / 2)
mod_su_bestfit <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]

mod_su_bestfit
mods_su_dAICc
```

```{r}
df_do_pred <- df_do %>%
  reframe(
    logsize_t0 = seq(
      min(logsize_t0),
      max(logsize_t0),
      length.out = 100)) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
    logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3) %>%
  mutate(
    enter_dormancy = predict(
      mod_do_bestfit,
      newdata = .,
      type = "response"))

fig_do_bin <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = df_do_bindata,
    aes(x = logsize_t0, y = enter_dormancy)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = df_do_bindata,
    aes(
      x = logsize_t0,
      ymin = lwr,
      ymax = upr),
    width = 0.1) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_do_pred,
    aes(x = logsize_t0, y = enter_dormancy),
    linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    x = expression("log(diameter)"[t0]),
    y = "") +
  theme_bw() +
  ylim(0, 1)

fig_do <- fig_do_line + fig_do_bin + plot_layout()
fig_do
```

### Reactivation
#### Data

```{r}
df_ra <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(reactivate),
         !is.na(disturbance))
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_ra_0 <- glm(
  reactivate ~ 1,
  data = df_ra, family = binomial)

mod_ra_1 <- glm(
  reactivate ~ disturbance,
  data = df_ra, family = binomial)

mods_ra <- list(
  mod_ra_0, mod_ra_1)

mods_ra_dAICc <- AICctab(
  mods_ra, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mod_ra_index_bestfit <- which.min(mods_ra_dAICc)
mod_ra_bestfit <- mods_ra[[mod_ra_index_bestfit]]

mod_ra_bestfit
mods_ra_dAICc

p_reactivate_0 <- predict(
  mod_ra_bestfit,
  newdata = data.frame(disturbance = 0),
  type = "response")[1]

p_reactivate_1 <- predict(
  mod_ra_bestfit,
  newdata = data.frame(disturbance = 1),
  type = "response")[1]

p_reactivate_0
p_reactivate_1

df_ra_size <- df %>%
  filter(
    reactivate == 1,
    size_reactivate_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_reactivate =
      log(size_reactivate_t1))

react_sz <- mean(
  df_ra_size$logsize_reactivate,
  na.rm = TRUE)

react_sd <- sd(
  df_ra_size$logsize_reactivate,
  na.rm = TRUE)
```

#### Plot
```{r}
df_ra_plot <- df_ra %>%

  mutate(
    lwr = binom.confint(

    disturbance_lab = factor(
```

### Flowering probability
#### Data
```{r}
df_fl <- df %>%
  filter(
    state == "active",
    !is.na(flower),

    is.finite(logsize_t0),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev))
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_fl_00 <- glm(
  flower ~ 1,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_0 <- glm(
  flower ~ disturbance_prev,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_10 <- glm(
  flower ~ logsize_t0,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_1 <- glm(
  flower ~ logsize_t0 + disturbance_prev,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_20 <- glm(
  flower ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_2 <- glm(
  flower ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + disturbance_prev,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_30 <- glm(
  flower ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mod_fl_3 <- glm(
  flower ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3 +
    disturbance_prev,
  data = df_fl, family = binomial)

mods_fl <- list(
  mod_fl_00, mod_fl_0, mod_fl_10, mod_fl_1,
  mod_fl_20, mod_fl_2, mod_fl_30, mod_fl_3)

mods_fl_dAICc <- AICctab(
  mods_fl, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

if (length(v_mod_set_fl) == 0) {
  mod_fl_index_bestfit <- which.min(mods_fl_dAICc)
} else {
  keep <- 2 * v_mod_set_fl + c(1, 2)
  mod_fl_index_bestfit <- keep[which.min(mods_fl_dAICc[keep])]
}

v_mod_fl_index <- floor((mod_fl_index_bestfit - 1) / 2)
mod_fl_bestfit <- mods_fl[[mod_fl_index_bestfit]]

mod_fl_bestfit
mods_fl_dAICc
```

### Recruitment 
#### Data
```{r}
df_sc2re <- df_re %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(nr_scapes),
    !is.na(recruits_simple)) %>%
  group_by(site, pop, year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_scapes = sum(nr_scapes),
    recruit_count = sum(recruits_simple),
    disturbance = case_when(
      any(disturbance == 1, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,
      any(is.na(disturbance)) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 0),
    disturbance_prev = case_when(
      any(disturbance_prev == 1, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,
      any(is.na(disturbance_prev)) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 0),
    .groups = "drop")

df_sc2re_mod <- df_sc2re %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(total_scapes),
    !is.na(recruit_count),
    !is.na(disturbance))
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_re_00 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ 1,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_0 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ disturbance,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_sc0 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ total_scapes,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_sc1 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ total_scapes + disturbance,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_sc2 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ total_scapes * disturbance,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_logsc0 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ log1p(total_scapes),
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_logsc1 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ log1p(total_scapes) + disturbance,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mod_re_logsc2 <- glm.nb(
  recruit_count ~ log1p(total_scapes) * disturbance,
  data = df_sc2re_mod)

mods_re <- list(
  mod_re_00, mod_re_0,
  mod_re_sc0, mod_re_sc1, mod_re_sc2,
  mod_re_logsc0, mod_re_logsc1, mod_re_logsc2)

mods_re_dAICc <- AICctab(
  mods_re, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mods_re_sorted <- order(mods_re_dAICc)
mod_re_index_bestfit <- mods_re_sorted[1]
mod_re_bestfit <- mods_re[[mod_re_index_bestfit]]

mod_re_bestfit
mods_re_dAICc
```

#### Mean recruitment conversion for the IPM
```{r}
# Predict recruitment for the same observed scape distribution under
```

## Parameters
### Extracting parameter estimates
```{r}
# Survival
coef_su <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_su_bestfit)),
  value = coef(mod_su_bestfit)) %>%
  mutate(
    coefficient = as.character(coefficient),
    coefficient = replace(
      coefficient, grepl("Intercept", coefficient), "b0"))

# Growth
coef_gr_fe <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_gr_bestfit)),
  value = coef(mod_gr_bestfit))

coef_gr_var <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_gr_var)),
  value = coef(mod_gr_var))

coef_gr <- bind_rows(coef_gr_fe, coef_gr_var) %>%
  mutate(
    coefficient = as.character(coefficient),
    coefficient = replace(
      coefficient, grepl("Intercept", coefficient), "b0"))

# Dormancy entry
coef_do <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_do_bestfit)),
  value = coef(mod_do_bestfit)) %>%
  mutate(
    coefficient = as.character(coefficient),
    coefficient = replace(
      coefficient, grepl("Intercept", coefficient), "b0"))

# Reactivation
coef_ra <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_ra_bestfit)),
  value = coef(mod_ra_bestfit)) %>%
  mutate(
    coefficient = as.character(coefficient),
    coefficient = replace(
      coefficient, grepl("Intercept", coefficient), "b0"))

# Flowering probability
coef_fl <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_fl_bestfit)),
  value = coef(mod_fl_bestfit)) %>%
  mutate(
    coefficient = as.character(coefficient),
    coefficient = replace(
      coefficient, grepl("Intercept", coefficient), "b0"))

# Scape number conditional on flowering
coef_fln <- data.frame(
  coefficient = names(coef(mod_fl_n_bestfit)),
  value = coef(mod_fl_n_bestfit)) %>%
  mutate(
    coefficient = as.character(coefficient),
    coefficient = replace(
      coefficient, grepl("Intercept", coefficient), "b0"))

extr_value <- function(x, field) {
  subset(x, coefficient == field)$value
}
```

### IPM constants
```{r}
mesh_limits <- range(

    df_gr$logsize_t0,
    df_gr$logsize_t1,
    df_re_size$logsize_t0,
    df_ra_size$logsize_reactivate),

  finite = TRUE)

  coefficient = c(
    "recr_sz",
    "recr_sd",
    "react_sz",
    "react_sd",
    "recr_0",
    "recr_1",
    "max_siz",
    "min_siz"),
  value = c(
    recr_sz,
    recr_sd,
    react_sz,
    react_sd,
    recr_per_scape_0,
    recr_per_scape_1,
    mesh_limits[2],
    mesh_limits[1]))
```

### Parameter list
```{r}
pars <- Filter(function(x) length(x) > 0, list(
  prefix = v_script_prefix,
  species = v_species,
  
  surv_b0 = extr_value(coef_su, "b0"),
  surv_b1 = extr_value(coef_su, "logsize_t0"),
  surv_b2 = extr_value(coef_su, "logsize_t0_2"),
  surv_b3 = extr_value(coef_su, "logsize_t0_3"),
  surv_bd = extr_value(coef_su, "disturbance"),
  
  grow_b0 = extr_value(coef_gr, "b0"),
  grow_b1 = extr_value(coef_gr, "logsize_t0"),
  grow_b2 = extr_value(coef_gr, "logsize_t0_2"),
  grow_b3 = extr_value(coef_gr, "logsize_t0_3"),
  grow_bd = extr_value(coef_gr, "disturbance"),
  a = extr_value(coef_gr, "a"),
  b = extr_value(coef_gr, "b"),
  
  dorm_b0 = extr_value(coef_do, "b0"),
  dorm_b1 = extr_value(coef_do, "logsize_t0"),
  dorm_b2 = extr_value(coef_do, "logsize_t0_2"),
  dorm_b3 = extr_value(coef_do, "logsize_t0_3"),
  dorm_bd = extr_value(coef_do, "disturbance"),
  
  react_b0 = extr_value(coef_ra, "b0"),
  react_bd = extr_value(coef_ra, "disturbance"),
  
  fl_b0 = extr_value(coef_fl, "b0"),
  fl_b1 = extr_value(coef_fl, "logsize_t0"),
  fl_b2 = extr_value(coef_fl, "logsize_t0_2"),
  fl_b3 = extr_value(coef_fl, "logsize_t0_3"),
  fl_bd = extr_value(coef_fl, "disturbance_prev"),
  
  fln_b0 = extr_value(coef_fln, "b0"),
  fln_b1 = extr_value(coef_fln, "logsize_t0"),
  fln_b2 = extr_value(coef_fln, "logsize_t0_2"),
  fln_b3 = extr_value(coef_fln, "logsize_t0_3"),
  fln_bd = extr_value(coef_fln, "disturbance_prev"),
  
  recr_0 = extr_value(coef_misc, "recr_0"),
  recr_1 = extr_value(coef_misc, "recr_1"),
  recr_sz = extr_value(coef_misc, "recr_sz"),
  recr_sd = extr_value(coef_misc, "recr_sd"),
  react_sz = extr_value(coef_misc, "react_sz"),
  react_sd = extr_value(coef_misc, "react_sd"),
  
  L = extr_value(coef_misc, "min_siz"),
  U = extr_value(coef_misc, "max_siz"),
  mat_siz = 200,
  
  mod_su_index = v_mod_su_index,
  mod_gr_index = v_mod_gr_index,
  mod_do_index = v_mod_do_index,
  mod_fl_index = v_mod_fl_index,
  mod_fl_n_index = v_mod_fl_n_index))
```

## Building the IPM
The demographic IPM consists of 200 continuous active-size classes and one
discrete dormant state. The resulting demographic kernel therefore has
dimensions $201 \times 201$.

For active individuals, survival is divided between remaining active and
entering dormancy. Individuals that remain active transition among size classes
according to the fitted growth distribution. Dormant individuals either remain
dormant or reactivate and return to the active size distribution. Fecundity
adds new recruits to the active portion of the kernel according to the fitted
recruit-size distribution.

The full demographic kernel can therefore be represented schematically as

$$
K =
\begin{bmatrix}
T + F & R \\
D & Z
\end{bmatrix},
$$

where $T$ contains survival and growth among active individuals, $F$ is the
fecundity kernel, $D$ represents entry into dormancy, $R$ represents
reactivation into the active state, and $Z$ represents continued dormancy.

### IPM functions
```{r}
inv_logit <- function(x) {
  exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))
}


# Survival ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sx <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance = 0,
    num_pars = pars$mod_su_index) {
  
  val <- pars$surv_b0
  
  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0("surv_b", i)
    
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }
  
  if (!is.null(pars$surv_bd)) {
    val <- val + pars$surv_bd * disturbance
  }
  
  inv_logit(val)
}


# Growth -----------------------------------------------------------------------
grow_mu <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance = 0,
    num_pars = pars$mod_gr_index) {
  
  val <- pars$grow_b0
  
  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0("grow_b", i)
    
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }
  
  if (!is.null(pars$grow_bd)) {
    val <- val + pars$grow_bd * disturbance
  }
  
  val
}


# Growth variation -------------------------------------------------------------
grow_sd <- function(mu, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * mu))
}


# Growth transition ------------------------------------------------------------
gxy <- function(x, y, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  mu <- grow_mu(
    x, pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = mu,
    sd = grow_sd(mu, pars))
}


# Dormancy entry ---------------------------------------------------------------
dorm_x <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance = 0,
    num_pars = pars$mod_do_index) {
  
  val <- pars$dorm_b0
  
  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0("dorm_b", i)
    
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }
  
  if (!is.null(pars$dorm_bd)) {
    val <- val + pars$dorm_bd * disturbance
  }
  
  inv_logit(val)
}


# Reactivation -----------------------------------------------------------------
react_p <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  val <- pars$react_b0
  
  if (!is.null(pars$react_bd)) {
    val <- val + pars$react_bd * disturbance
  }
  
  inv_logit(val)
}


# Flowering probability --------------------------------------------------------
fl_x <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0,
    num_pars = pars$mod_fl_index) {
  
  val <- pars$fl_b0
  
  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0("fl_b", i)
    
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }
  
  if (!is.null(pars$fl_bd)) {
    val <- val + pars$fl_bd * disturbance_prev
  }
  
  inv_logit(val)
}


# Scape number conditional on flowering ---------------------------------------
fl_n_x <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0,
    num_pars = pars$mod_fl_n_index) {
  
  val <- pars$fln_b0
  
  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0("fln_b", i)
    
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }
  
  if (!is.null(pars$fln_bd)) {
    val <- val + pars$fln_bd * disturbance_prev
  }
  
  exp(val)
}


# Recruitment conversion -------------------------------------------------------
recruits_per_scape <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  if (disturbance == 0) {
    pars$recr_0
  } else {
    pars$recr_1
  }
}

# Recruitment size distribution ------------------------------------------------
re_y_dist <- function(y, pars) {
  norm <- pnorm(
    pars$U, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd) -
    pnorm(
      pars$L, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd)
  
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = pars$recr_sz,
    sd = pars$recr_sd) / norm
}


# Reactivation size distribution -----------------------------------------------
react_y_dist <- function(y, pars) {
  norm <- pnorm(
    pars$U, mean = pars$react_sz, sd = pars$react_sd) -
    pnorm(
      pars$L, mean = pars$react_sz, sd = pars$react_sd)
  
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = pars$react_sz,
    sd = pars$react_sd) / norm
}


# F-kernel ---------------------------------------------------------------------
fyx <- function(
    y, x, pars,
    disturbance = 0,
    disturbance_prev = 0) {
  
  fl_x(
    x, pars,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev) *
    fl_n_x(
      x, pars,
      disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev) *
    recruits_per_scape(
      pars,
      disturbance = disturbance) *
    re_y_dist(y, pars)
}
```

### Kernel
```{r}
kernel <- function(
    pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  # Active survival and dormancy
  Smat <- sx(
    y, pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  Dmat <- dorm_x(
    y, pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  # Growth
  Gmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  Gmat[] <- t(outer(
    y, y,
    Vectorize(function(x, y) {
      gxy(
        x, y, pars,
        disturbance = disturbance)
    }))) * h
  
  # Correct growth eviction
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (i <= n / 2) {
      Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    } else {
      Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    }
  }
  
  # Active -> active
  Tmat <- sweep(
    Gmat,
    2,
    Smat * (1 - Dmat),
    "*")
  
  # Active -> dormant
  Dorm_row <- matrix(
    Smat * Dmat,
    nrow = 1)
  
  # Dormant -> active
  React_vec <- react_y_dist(y, pars) * h
  React_vec <- React_vec / sum(React_vec)
  
  p_react <- react_p(
    pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  React_col <- matrix(
    p_react * React_vec,
    ncol = 1)
  
  # Dormant -> dormant
  Dorm_stasis <- 1 - p_react
  
  # Fertility
  Fmat <- outer(
    y, y,
    Vectorize(function(y, x) {
      fyx(
        y, x, pars,
        disturbance = disturbance,
        disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
    })) * h
  
  # Full 201 x 201 demographic kernel
  K <- rbind(
    cbind(Tmat + Fmat, React_col),
    cbind(Dorm_row, Dorm_stasis))
  
  return(list(
    k_yx = K,
    Fmat = Fmat,
    Tmat = Tmat,
    Gmat = Gmat,
    Dorm_row = Dorm_row,
    React_col = React_col,
    Smat = Smat,
    Dmat = Dmat,
    p_reactivate = p_react,
    meshpts = y,
    h = h))
}
```

### Population growth rate
```{r}
lambda_ipm <- function(
    pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  
  Re(eigen(
    kernel(
      pars,
      disturbance = disturbance,
      disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)$k_yx,
    only.values = TRUE)$values[1])
}
```

## Disturbance history
The four fixed disturbance kernels describe demographic outcomes under
specific disturbance histories but do not describe how frequently those
histories occur. The observed disturbance record was therefore used to
estimate transition probabilities between environmental states.

Across observed quadrat-year transitions, the probability of remaining
undisturbed following an undisturbed interval was 0.943, whereas the
probability of current disturbance was 0.057. Following a previously disturbed
interval, the probability of another disturbance was higher, at 0.205, while
the probability of returning to an undisturbed interval was 0.795.

Previous disturbance was uncommon overall: approximately 93.1% of observed
quadrat-years had no disturbance in the preceding interval and 6.9% had
previous disturbance. These frequencies are used only to initialize the
environmental-history population vector, whereas the conditional transition
probabilities determine movement between environmental states during repeated
```{r}
df_disturbance_regime <- df_re_all %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev)) %>%
  distinct(
    site, pop, qu, year,
    disturbance, disturbance_prev) %>%
  count(
    disturbance,
    disturbance_prev,
    name = "n_quadrat_years") %>%
  complete(
    disturbance = c(0, 1),
    disturbance_prev = c(0, 1),
    fill = list(n_quadrat_years = 0)) %>%
  arrange(
    disturbance_prev,
    disturbance)

df_disturbance_regime
```

## State-specific demographic kernels
Current and previous disturbance enter different components of the demographic
kernel. Current disturbance can affect demographic transitions occurring from
$t$ to $t+1$, including growth, reactivation, and recruitment. Previous
disturbance can affect reproduction observed at time $t$, most importantly
flowering probability.

The full IPM must therefore distinguish four combinations of disturbance
history. We denote a demographic kernel by $K_{ij}$, where the first index
indicates current disturbance during $t$ to $t+1$ and the second indicates
previous disturbance during $t-1$ to $t$. Thus,

$$
K_{00}
$$

represents no fire in either interval,

$$
K_{10}
$$

represents current fire only,

$$
K_{01}
$$

represents previous fire only, and

$$
K_{11}
$$

represents fire in both intervals.

Although individual vital-rate models generally contain either current or
previous disturbance, both disturbance variables occur together in the full
fecundity and demographic kernels. This allows the immediate recruitment
response to fire and the lagged flowering response to fire to operate
simultaneously.
```{r}
K_00_obj <- kernel(
  pars,
  disturbance = 0,
  disturbance_prev = 0)

K_10_obj <- kernel(
  pars,
  disturbance = 1,
  disturbance_prev = 0)

K_01_obj <- kernel(
  pars,
  disturbance = 0,
  disturbance_prev = 1)

K_11_obj <- kernel(
  pars,
  disturbance = 1,
  disturbance_prev = 1)

K_00 <- K_00_obj$k_yx
K_10 <- K_10_obj$k_yx
K_01 <- K_01_obj$k_yx
K_11 <- K_11_obj$k_yx
```

## Environmental historical megamatrix
```{r}
K_env_hist <- rbind(
  cbind(
    p_0_given_0 * K_00,
    p_0_given_1 * K_01),
  cbind(
    p_1_given_0 * K_10,
    p_1_given_1 * K_11))
```

## Environmental historical asymptotic lambda
To retain disturbance history through time, the demographic state space is
duplicated for the two possible previous-disturbance states. Each environmental
state contains the complete 201-state demographic IPM, giving an
environmental-history projection matrix of dimension $402 \times 402$.

The environmental-history matrix is

$$
K_{\mathrm{env}} =
\begin{bmatrix}
P(0 \mid 0)K_{00} & P(0 \mid 1)K_{01} \\
P(1 \mid 0)K_{10} & P(1 \mid 1)K_{11}
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Columns identify the disturbance state inherited from the preceding interval,
whereas rows identify disturbance during the current interval. Current
disturbance then becomes the previous-disturbance state for the following
projection. In this way, demographic dynamics and the observed temporal
dependence of disturbance are propagated simultaneously.
```{r}
lambda_env_hist <- Re(
  eigen(
    K_env_hist,
    only.values = TRUE)$values[1])

lambda_env_hist
```

## Mean observed population structure
```{r}
make_initial_n_mean <- function(pars, df_init = df_ind) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  
  breaks <- seq(
    L, U,
    length.out = n + 1)
  
  years_i <- df_init %>%
    filter(state %in% c("active", "dormant")) %>%
    distinct(year) %>%
    arrange(year) %>%
    pull(year)
  
  counts_by_year <- map(years_i, function(year_i) {
    df_i <- df_init %>%
      filter(year == year_i)
    
    active_size <- df_i %>%
      filter(
        state == "active",
        is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
      pull(logsize_t0)
    
    active_counts <- hist(
      pmin(pmax(active_size, L), U),
      breaks = breaks,
      plot = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE)$counts
    
    dormant_count <- sum(
      df_i$state == "dormant",
      na.rm = TRUE)
    
    c(active_counts, dormant_count)
  })
  
  Reduce(`+`, counts_by_year) / length(counts_by_year)
}

n_obs <- make_initial_n_mean(pars)
```

## Initial environmental-history population
```{r}
n_env_initial <- c(
  p_prev_0 * n_obs,
  p_prev_1 * n_obs)
```

## One-step projection
```{r}
project_kernel <- function(K, n_initial, label) {
  n_initial_total <- sum(n_initial)
  
  n_proj <- as.numeric(
    K %*% n_initial)
  
  n_projected <- sum(n_proj)
  
  tibble(
    lambda_type = label,
    asym_lambda = Re(
      eigen(
        K,
        only.values = TRUE)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = n_projected / n_initial_total,
    n_initial = n_initial_total,
    n_projected = n_projected)
}
```

## Fixed disturbance-state lambdas
```{r}
df_lambda_states <- bind_rows(
  project_kernel(
    K_00,
    n_obs,
    "Undisturbed") %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance = 0,
      disturbance_prev = 0),
  
  project_kernel(
    K_10,
    n_obs,
    "Current-year fire") %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance = 1,
      disturbance_prev = 0),
  
  project_kernel(
    K_01,
    n_obs,
    "Previous-year fire") %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance = 0,
      disturbance_prev = 1),
  
  project_kernel(
    K_11,
    n_obs,
    "Fire in both years") %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance = 1,
      disturbance_prev = 1))

df_lambda_states
```

```{r}
# Count known living individuals. New adults are additionally counted one year
# earlier, matching the simplified recruitment assumption used in this IPM.

df_counts_alive <- df_ind %>%
  filter(state %in% c("active", "dormant", "alive_or_dormant")) %>%
  count(site, pop, qu, year, name = "n_alive")

df_newadult_backfill <- df_ind %>%
  filter(recruit_type == "new_adult") %>%
  transmute(site, pop, qu, year = year - 1) %>%
  count(site, pop, qu, year, name = "n_newadult_backfill")

# Use recruitment rows as the monitored quadrat-year inventory
df_counts_quad <- df %>%
  filter(row_type == "recruitment") %>%
  distinct(site, pop, qu, year) %>%
  left_join(
    df_counts_alive,
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  left_join(
    df_newadult_backfill,
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    n_alive = replace_na(n_alive, 0L),
    n_newadult_backfill = replace_na(n_newadult_backfill, 0L),
    n = n_alive + n_newadult_backfill) %>%
  group_by(site, pop, qu) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n),
    annual_transition = year_t1 == year + 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(annual_transition)

# The final three transitions cannot fully resolve terminal dormancy
dormancy_cutoff <- 3
last_complete_transition <- max(df_ind$year, na.rm = TRUE) -
  dormancy_cutoff - 1

df_counts_year <- df_counts_quad %>%
  filter(year <= last_complete_transition) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quads = n(),
    n_t0 = sum(n),
    n_t1 = sum(n_t1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lambda_obs = n_t1 / n_t0)

df_counts_year

# Mean observed population growth

lam_obs_mean <- mean(lam_obs_y, na.rm = TRUE)
lam_obs_geo <- exp(mean(log(lam_obs_y), na.rm = TRUE))

lam_obs_mean
```

# Investigations 01 {#invest01}

## Presumed second-year recruits

Recruitment is not always observed at the seedling stage. Individuals first
recorded with `s = 5` are explicitly identified as seedlings, whereas individuals
first appearing with `s = 3` enter the demographic record as new adults. In the
recruitment reconstruction, these new adults are interpreted as recruits that
were not detected during their seedling year and are therefore assigned to an
earlier recruitment cohort.

The clearest cases supporting this interpretation are new adults that enter as
stage 2. These individuals are treated here as *presumed second-year recruits*.
Before using this interpretation in the IPM, we examined whether their sizes at
entry are consistent with the sizes actually reached by known seedlings one
year after their observed seedling census.

The purpose of this analysis is diagnostic only. No recruit classifications or
recorded sizes are changed.


```{r presumed-recruits-run, include=FALSE}
# Raw demographic data --------------------------------------------------------
df_recruit_og <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    dir_data,
    "eriogonum_longifolium_data.csv"),
  col_types = cols(
    comment = col_character())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(
      str_sub(date, 1, 4)),
    month = as.numeric(
      str_sub(date, 6, 7)),
    id = str_c(
      site, pop, qu, plant,
      sep = "_"),
    record_type = case_when(
      !is.na(s) ~ "demography",
      is.na(s) & !is.na(burn) ~ "burn",
      TRUE ~ "other"))


df_recruit_demog <- df_recruit_og %>%
  filter(
    record_type == "demography")


df_recruit_june <- df_recruit_demog %>%
  filter(
    month == 6)


# First year in which each quadrat was monitored -------------------------------
df_recruit_quad_start <- df_recruit_june %>%
  group_by(
    site, pop, qu) %>%
  summarise(
    first_quad_year = min(year),
    .groups = "drop")


# First recruitment record for each individual --------------------------------
df_recruit_first_diag <- df_recruit_demog %>%
  filter(
    s %in% c(3, 5)) %>%
  arrange(
    id, year, month) %>%
  distinct(
    id,
    .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    recruit_year = if_else(
      month > 6,
      year + 1,
      year)) %>%
  left_join(
    df_recruit_quad_start,
    by = c(
      "site",
      "pop",
      "qu")) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline =
      recruit_year ==
      first_quad_year,
    recruit_type = case_when(
      s == 5 ~ "seedling",
      s == 3 ~ "new_adult"),
    recruit_class = case_when(
      s == 5 ~
        "observed_seedling",
      s == 3 & stage == 2 ~
        "presumed_2yr",
      s == 3 ~
        "new_adult_other")) %>%
  filter(
    !baseline)


# Annual active-to-active transitions -----------------------------------------
df_recruit_transition <- df_recruit_june %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    s_t1 = lead(s),
    dia_t1 = lead(dia),
    annual_transition =
      year_t1 == year + 1,
    active_t0 =
      s %in% c(1, 3, 5),
    active_t1 =
      s_t1 %in% c(1, 3, 5),
    size_t0 = if_else(
      active_t0,
      dia,
      NA_real_),
    size_t1 = if_else(
      annual_transition &
        active_t0 &
        active_t1,
      dia_t1,
      NA_real_)) %>%
  ungroup()


# Recruit entries linked to annual size histories -----------------------------
df_recruit_entry_diag <- df_recruit_first_diag %>%
  transmute(
    site,
    pop,
    qu,
    plant,
    id,
    recruit_year,
    recruit_type,
    recruit_class,
    stage_entry = stage,
    raw_entry_dia = dia) %>%
  left_join(
    df_recruit_transition %>%
      dplyr::select(
        id,
        year,
        size_t0,
        size_t1),
    by = c(
      "id",
      "recruit_year" = "year"))


# Recruit-class counts ---------------------------------------------------------
df_recruit_class_summary <- df_recruit_entry_diag %>%
  count(
    recruit_class,
    name = "n") %>%
  mutate(
    Recruit_class = recode(
      recruit_class,
      observed_seedling =
        "Observed seedlings",
      presumed_2yr =
        "Presumed second-year recruits",
      new_adult_other =
        "Other new-adult entries")) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Recruit_class,
    N = n)


# Empirical second-year sizes --------------------------------------------------
# Known seedlings:
# size at t + 1 after an observed seedling census.
#
# Presumed second-year recruits:
# size at first annual census as a stage-2 new adult.

df_year2_size <- bind_rows(
  df_recruit_entry_diag %>%
    filter(
      recruit_class ==
        "observed_seedling",
      size_t1 > 0) %>%
    transmute(
      id,
      source =

      year2_size = size_t1),

  df_recruit_entry_diag %>%
    filter(
      recruit_class ==
        "presumed_2yr",
      size_t0 > 0) %>%
    transmute(
      id,
      source =
        "Presumed second-year recruits",
      year2_size = size_t0)) %>%
  mutate(
    log_year2_size =
      log(year2_size))


# Size-distribution summary ---------------------------------------------------
df_year2_size_summary <- df_year2_size %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(year2_size),
    median = median(year2_size),

    q75 = quantile(

# Size comparison figure ------------------------------------------------------
fig_year2_recruit_size <- ggplot(

n_presumed_growth <- nrow(

n_presumed_lt1 <- df_recruit_entry_diag %>%
```

The first-record classifications are summarized below. Baseline individuals
already present when a quadrat entered monitoring are excluded because their
recruitment timing cannot be inferred from their first database record.

```{r presumed-recruit-counts, echo=FALSE}
df_recruit_class_summary %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


### Are presumed second-year recruits plausible second-year plants?

For observed seedlings with a subsequent active annual census, the size at the
following census provides an empirical distribution of second-year plant sizes.
This distribution can be compared directly with the entry sizes of stage-2 new
adults interpreted as presumed second-year recruits.

```{r presumed-recruit-size-table, echo=FALSE}
df_year2_size_summary %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        mean,
        median,
        sd,
        q25,
        q75,
        min,
        max),
      ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  rename(
    Group = source,
    N = n,
    Mean = mean,
    Median = median,
    SD = sd,
    `25%` = q25,
    `75%` = q75,
    Minimum = min,
    Maximum = max) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r presumed-recruit-size-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
fig_year2_recruit_size
```


The size distributions provide no indication that the stage-2 new adults form
an artificial group of exceptionally small observations. Instead, their entry
sizes overlap the size range reached by individuals that were directly observed
as seedlings in the preceding year. This supports the interpretation of these
stage-2 new adults as plausible second-year recruits, while recognizing that
their actual seedling census was not observed.


### Subsequent growth

There were `r n_presumed_2yr` presumed second-year recruit entries. Of these,
`r n_presumed_growth` had a positive active size measurement in the following
annual census and could therefore be compared with the complete annual growth
dataset.

```{r presumed-recruit-growth-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
fig_presumed_growth
```


The highlighted observations show the growth transitions beginning at presumed
second-year recruit entry. Their subsequent growth falls within the broader
annual growth distribution rather than forming a clearly separate growth
process.

Only `r n_presumed_lt1` presumed second-year recruits entered the annual data
below 1 cm. Thus, the later issue of extremely small non-seedling measurements
is not primarily generated by the reconstruction of presumed second-year
recruits.

Overall, the available size and growth information is consistent with retaining
stage-2 new adults as presumed second-year recruits. The assumption nevertheless
remains inferential because their seedling stage was not directly observed.
A separate sensitivity analysis can therefore test how recruitment and
population growth change when these reconstructed recruits are included or
excluded.



## Dormancy and uncertainty in terminal survival

Dormancy is an important component of the life history of *Eriogonum
longifolium*. Individuals may remain belowground for one or more annual censuses
before reappearing aboveground. Consequently, the disappearance of an
individual from a census cannot automatically be interpreted as mortality.

During construction of the working data, absences occurring between two known
living observations were retrospectively classified as dormancy. These cases
are unambiguous because subsequent reappearance demonstrates that the individual
had remained alive. In total, 409 reconstructed dormancy spells were identified
among 344 individuals. Most were short: 76.5% lasted one year, 90.5% no more
than two years, and 94.9% no more than three years. Nevertheless, substantially
longer dormant periods occurred, including a maximum reconstructed interval of
20 years.

The main uncertainty therefore concerns individuals disappearing near the end
of the study. Unlike earlier absences, these records cannot be resolved
retrospectively because there are insufficient subsequent censuses to determine
whether an individual died or remained dormant. In the working data, three
years was adopted as the default operational cutoff. An absence of up to three
years at the end of the record is treated as unresolved rather than as mortality.
The three-year threshold captures 388 of the 409 observed dormancy spells
(94.9%) and is therefore intended as a pragmatic classification rule rather than
as a biological maximum duration of dormancy.

### Sensitivity to the dormancy cutoff

Because the treatment of terminal absences directly affects estimated survival
and the years for which observed population growth can be considered complete,
we evaluated the sensitivity of the results to this assumption. The maximum
allowable period of unresolved dormancy was varied from 0 to 20 years, with
three years retained as the reference scenario.

For each cutoff, active individuals followed by an unresolved absence spell
longer than the specified cutoff were classified as dead, whereas shorter
terminal absences remained unresolved. The survival model was then refitted and
the mean IPM rebuilt. Independently, observed annual population growth was
recalculated after excluding terminal transitions for which the selected
dormancy allowance prevented mortality from being resolved. Confirmed dormancy
and reactivation observations, as well as observed growth, flowering and
recruitment data, were retained throughout the analysis.


```{r}
# Sensitivity specification ----------------------------------------------------
v_mod_set_su <- c()
v_mod_set_gr <- c()
v_mod_set_do <- c()
v_mod_set_fl <- c()
v_mod_set_fl_n <- c()

dormancy_cutoffs <- 0:20
reference_cutoff <- 3

v_ggp_suffix <- "Archbold - Eriogonum longifolium"
```


```{r dormancy-sensitivity-run, include=FALSE}
# Raw data ---------------------------------------------------------------------
df_og <- read_csv(
  file.path(dir_data, "eriogonum_longifolium_data.csv"),
  col_types = cols(comment = col_character())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(str_sub(date, 1, 4)),
    month = as.numeric(str_sub(date, 6, 7)),
    id = str_c(site, pop, qu, plant, sep = "_"),
    record_type = case_when(
      !is.na(s) ~ "demography",
      is.na(s) & !is.na(burn) ~ "burn",
      TRUE ~ "other"))

df_demog <- df_og %>%
  filter(record_type == "demography")

df_demog_june <- df_demog %>%
  filter(month == 6)


# Clean annual demographic history --------------------------------------------
# Absences bracketed by known living observations are confirmed dormancy.
# These remain dormant under every sensitivity scenario.

df_alive_range <- df_demog_june %>%
  filter(s %in% c(1, 3, 5)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    first_alive = min(year),
    last_alive = max(year), .groups = "drop")

df_annual <- df_demog_june %>%
  left_join(df_alive_range, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(
    dormancy_repair = s %in% c(0, 9) &
      !is.na(first_alive) & year > first_alive & year < last_alive,
    s_clean = if_else(dormancy_repair, 8, s),
    stage_clean = if_else(dormancy_repair, 5, stage),
    state_clean = case_when(
      s_clean %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ "active",
      s_clean == 8 ~ "dormant",
      s_clean == 10 ~ "alive_or_dormant",
      s_clean == 0 ~ "absent",
      s_clean == 9 ~ "previous_absent",
      s_clean %in% c(2, 6, 7) ~ "missing",
      s_clean == 11 ~ "discontinued",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_))


# Unresolved absence spells ----------------------------------------------------
df_absence_spell <- df_annual %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    absent_state = state_clean %in% c("absent", "previous_absent"),
    new_spell = row_number() == 1 |
      coalesce(absent_state != lag(absent_state), TRUE) |
      coalesce(year != lag(year) + 1, TRUE),
    spell = cumsum(new_spell)) %>%
  group_by(id, spell) %>%
  summarise(
    absent_state = first(absent_state),
    absence_start = min(year),
    absence_end = max(year),
    absence_years = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(absent_state)

df_absence_t1 <- df_absence_spell %>%
  transmute(
    id,
    year_t1 = absence_start,
    absence_years)


# Base annual transitions ------------------------------------------------------
df_transition_base <- df_annual %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    annual_transition = coalesce(year_t1 == year + 1, FALSE),
    stage_t1 = if_else(
      annual_transition, lead(stage_clean), NA_real_),
    state_t1 = if_else(
      annual_transition, lead(state_clean), NA_character_),
    size_t0 = if_else(state_clean == "active", dia, NA_real_),
    size_t1 = if_else(
      annual_transition & state_clean == "active" &
        lead(state_clean) == "active",
      lead(dia), NA_real_),
    size_reactivate_t1 = if_else(
      annual_transition & state_clean == "dormant" &
        lead(state_clean) == "active",
      lead(dia), NA_real_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(df_absence_t1, by = c("id", "year_t1"))


# Recruitment structure --------------------------------------------------------
df_quad_start <- df_demog_june %>%
  group_by(site, pop, qu) %>%
  summarise(first_quad_year = min(year), .groups = "drop")

df_recruit_first <- df_demog %>%
  filter(s %in% c(3, 5)) %>%
  arrange(id, year, month) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    recruit_year = if_else(month > 6, year + 1, year)) %>%
  left_join(df_quad_start, by = c("site", "pop", "qu")) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline = recruit_year == first_quad_year,
    recruit_type = case_when(
      s == 5 ~ "seedling",
      s == 3 ~ "new_adult"))

df_quad_monitor <- df_annual %>%
  group_by(site, pop, qu, year) %>%
  summarise(
    monitored = any(state_clean != "discontinued", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(monitored) %>%
  select(-monitored)

df_recruit_followup <- df_quad_monitor %>%
  left_join(
    df_quad_monitor %>%
      transmute(
        site, pop, qu, year = year - 1,
        monitored_t1 = TRUE),
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  left_join(
    df_quad_monitor %>%
      transmute(
        site, pop, qu, year = year - 2,
        monitored_t2 = TRUE),
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    monitored_t1 = replace_na(monitored_t1, FALSE),
    monitored_t2 = replace_na(monitored_t2, FALSE))

df_recruit_count_simple <- df_recruit_first %>%
  filter(!baseline) %>%
  mutate(
    fecundity_year_simple = case_when(
      recruit_type == "seedling" ~ recruit_year - 1,
      recruit_type == "new_adult" ~ recruit_year - 2)) %>%
  semi_join(
    df_quad_monitor,
    by = c(
      "site", "pop", "qu",
      "fecundity_year_simple" = "year")) %>%
  count(
    site, pop, qu, fecundity_year_simple, recruit_type,
    name = "nr_recruits") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = recruit_type,
    values_from = nr_recruits,
    values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(
    observed_seedling_simple = seedling,
    new_adult_simple = new_adult)

df_repro_quad <- df_quad_monitor %>%
  left_join(
    df_annual %>%
      filter(state_clean != "discontinued") %>%
      group_by(site, pop, qu, year) %>%
      summarise(
        nr_active = sum(state_clean == "active", na.rm = TRUE),
        nr_flower_obs = sum(
          state_clean == "active" & !is.na(scape), na.rm = TRUE),
        scape_sum = sum(
          if_else(state_clean == "active", scape, NA_real_),
          na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(
        nr_scapes = case_when(
          nr_active == 0 ~ 0,
          nr_flower_obs == 0 ~ NA_real_,
          TRUE ~ scape_sum)) %>%
      select(site, pop, qu, year, nr_active, nr_scapes),
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year"))

df_recruit_quad <- df_recruit_followup %>%
  left_join(
    df_recruit_count_simple,
    by = c(
      "site", "pop", "qu",
      "year" = "fecundity_year_simple")) %>%
  left_join(
    df_repro_quad,
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    observed_seedling_simple = case_when(
      monitored_t1 ~ replace_na(observed_seedling_simple, 0L),
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
    new_adult_simple = case_when(
      monitored_t2 ~ replace_na(new_adult_simple, 0L),
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
    recruitment_complete = monitored_t1 & monitored_t2,
    recruits_simple = case_when(
      recruitment_complete ~
        observed_seedling_simple + new_adult_simple,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_))

df_recruit <- df_recruit_quad %>%
  transmute(
    row_type = "recruitment",
    site, pop, qu, year,
    recruitment_complete,
    recruits_simple,
    nr_scapes)

df_recruit_ind <- df_recruit_first %>%
  filter(!baseline) %>%
  transmute(
    id,
    year = recruit_year,
    recruit_type)


# Scenario-specific workdata ---------------------------------------------------
make_scenario_data <- function(dormancy_cutoff) {
  
  df_transition <- df_transition_base %>%
    mutate(
      survives = case_when(
        !annual_transition ~ NA_real_,
        !state_clean %in% c("active", "dormant") ~ NA_real_,
        state_t1 %in%
          c("active", "dormant", "alive_or_dormant") ~ 1,
        state_t1 %in% c("absent", "previous_absent") &
          absence_years > dormancy_cutoff ~ 0,
        state_t1 %in% c("absent", "previous_absent") &
          absence_years <= dormancy_cutoff ~ NA_real_,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_),
      
      enter_dormancy = case_when(
        state_clean != "active" | survives != 1 ~ NA_real_,
        state_t1 == "dormant" ~ 1,
        state_t1 == "active" ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_),
      
      reactivate = case_when(
        state_clean != "dormant" ~ NA_real_,
        state_t1 == "active" ~ 1,
        state_t1 == "dormant" ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_),
      
      flower = case_when(
        state_clean != "active" ~ NA_real_,
        !is.na(scape) & scape > 0 ~ 1,
        !is.na(scape) & scape == 0 ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_),
      
      fl_nr = if_else(
        state_clean == "active", scape, NA_real_),
      logsize_t0 = log(size_t0),
      logsize_t1 = log(size_t1),
      logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
      logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3)
  
  df_ind <- df_transition %>%
    left_join(df_recruit_ind, by = c("id", "year")) %>%
    transmute(
      row_type = "individual",
      site, pop, qu, id, year,
      state = state_clean,
      state_t1,
      stage = stage_clean,
      stage_t1,
      survives,
      enter_dormancy,
      recruit_type,
      size_reactivate_t1,
      reactivate,
      size_t0,
      size_t1,
      logsize_t0,
      logsize_t1,
      logsize_t0_2,
      logsize_t0_3,
      flower,
      fl_nr)
  
  bind_rows(df_ind, df_recruit) %>%
    mutate(
      row_type = as.character(row_type),
      year = as.numeric(year))
}


# Model helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------
poly_formulas <- function(response) {
  list(
    as.formula(paste(response, '~ 1')),
    as.formula(paste(response, '~ logsize_t0')),
    as.formula(paste(
      response, '~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2')),
    as.formula(paste(
      response,
      '~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3')))
}

get_daicc <- function(mods) {
  aicc <- sapply(mods, function(mod) {
    k <- attr(logLik(mod), "df")
    n <- nobs(mod)
    AIC(mod) + 2 * k * (k + 1) / (n - k - 1)
  })
  
  aicc - min(aicc)
}

pick_model <- function(mods, manual = c()) {
  d_aicc <- get_daicc(mods)
  index <- if (length(manual) == 0) {
    which.min(d_aicc)
  } else {
    manual[1] + 1
  }

  list(
    model = mods[[index]],
    index = index - 1,
    d_aicc = d_aicc)
}

fit_poly_glm <- function(data, response, manual = c()) {
  forms <- poly_formulas(response)
  mods <- lapply(
    forms,
    function(form) glm(form, data = data, family = 'binomial'))
  pick_model(mods, manual)
}

fit_poly_lm <- function(data, response, manual = c()) {
  forms <- poly_formulas(response)
  mods <- lapply(forms, function(form) lm(form, data = data))
  pick_model(mods, manual)
}

fit_poly_nb <- function(data, response, manual = c()) {
  forms <- poly_formulas(response)
  mods <- lapply(forms, function(form) MASS::glm.nb(form, data = data))
  pick_model(mods, manual)
}

get_coef <- function(model, term) {
  values <- coef(model)
  if (term %in% names(values)) {
    unname(values[[term]])
  } else {
    NULL
  }
}


# IPM functions ----------------------------------------------------------------
inv_logit <- function(x) {
  exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))
}

sx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = pars$mod_su_index) {
  val <- pars$surv_b0

  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0('surv_b', i)
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }

  inv_logit(val)
}

grow_mu <- function(x, pars, num_pars = pars$mod_gr_index) {
  val <- pars$grow_b0

  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0('grow_b', i)
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }

  val
}

grow_sd <- function(mu, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * mu))
}

gxy <- function(x, y, pars) {
  mu <- grow_mu(x, pars)
  dnorm(y, mean = mu, sd = grow_sd(mu, pars))
}

dorm_x <- function(x, pars, num_pars = pars$mod_do_index) {
  val <- pars$dorm_b0

  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0('dorm_b', i)
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }

  inv_logit(val)
}

fl_x <- function(x, pars, num_pars = pars$mod_fl_index) {
  val <- pars$fl_b0

  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0('fl_b', i)
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }

  inv_logit(val)
}

fl_n_x <- function(x, pars, num_pars = pars$mod_fl_n_index) {
  val <- pars$fln_b0

  for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
    param <- paste0('fln_b', i)
    if (!is.null(pars[[param]])) {
      val <- val + pars[[param]] * x^i
    }
  }

  exp(val)
}

re_y_dist <- function(y, pars) {
  norm <- pnorm(
    pars$U, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd) -
    pnorm(
      pars$L, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd)

  dnorm(
    y, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd) / norm
}

react_y_dist <- function(y, pars) {
  norm <- pnorm(
    pars$U, mean = pars$react_sz, sd = pars$react_sd) -
    pnorm(
      pars$L, mean = pars$react_sz, sd = pars$react_sd)

  dnorm(
    y, mean = pars$react_sz, sd = pars$react_sd) / norm
}

fyx <- function(y, x, pars) {
  fl_x(x, pars) *
    fl_n_x(x, pars) *
    pars$fecu_b0 *
    re_y_dist(y, pars)
}

kernel <- function(pars) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n

  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])

  Smat <- sx(y, pars)
  Dmat <- dorm_x(y, pars)

  Gmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  Gmat[] <- t(outer(y, y, gxy, pars)) * h

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (i <= n / 2) {
      Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    } else {
      Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    }
  }

  Tmat <- sweep(
    Gmat, 2, Smat * (1 - Dmat), '*')

  Dorm_row <- matrix(
    Smat * Dmat, nrow = 1)

  React_vec <- react_y_dist(y, pars) * h
  React_vec <- React_vec / sum(React_vec)

  React_col <- matrix(
    pars$p_reactivate * React_vec, ncol = 1)

  Dorm_stasis <- 1 - pars$p_reactivate

  Fmat <- outer(
    y, y,
    Vectorize(function(y, x) {
      fyx(y, x, pars)
    })) * h

  K <- rbind(
    cbind(Tmat + Fmat, React_col),
    cbind(Dorm_row, Dorm_stasis))

  K
}

lambda_ipm <- function(pars) {
  Re(eigen(
    kernel(pars), only.values = TRUE)$values[1])
}


# Reference data for scenario-independent population counts -------------------
df_reference <- make_scenario_data(reference_cutoff)

df_ind_reference <- df_reference %>%
  filter(row_type == "individual")

max_ind_year <- max(df_annual$year, na.rm = TRUE)


# Observed population counts ---------------------------------------------------
df_counts_alive <- df_ind_reference %>%
  filter(state %in% c("active", "dormant", "alive_or_dormant")) %>%
  count(site, pop, qu, year, name = "n_alive")

df_newadult_backfill <- df_ind_reference %>%
  filter(recruit_type == "new_adult") %>%
  transmute(site, pop, qu, year = year - 1) %>%
  count(site, pop, qu, year, name = "n_newadult_backfill")

df_counts_quad <- df_reference %>%
  filter(row_type == "recruitment") %>%
  distinct(site, pop, qu, year) %>%
  left_join(
    df_counts_alive,
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  left_join(
    df_newadult_backfill,
    by = c("site", "pop", "qu", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    n_alive = replace_na(n_alive, 0L),
    n_newadult_backfill = replace_na(n_newadult_backfill, 0L),
    n = n_alive + n_newadult_backfill) %>%
  group_by(site, pop, qu) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n),
    annual_transition = year_t1 == year + 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(annual_transition)


# One sensitivity scenario -----------------------------------------------------
run_dormancy_scenario <- function(dormancy_cutoff) {
  
  df_i <- make_scenario_data(dormancy_cutoff)
  
  df_ind_i <- df_i %>%
    filter(row_type == "individual")
  
  df_re_i <- df_i %>%
    filter(
      row_type == "recruitment",
      recruitment_complete,
      !is.na(recruits_simple))
  
  
  # Survival -------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_su_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      state == "active",
      !is.na(survives),
      size_t0 > 0,
      is.finite(logsize_t0))
  
  fit_su_i <- fit_poly_glm(
    df_su_i, "survives", v_mod_set_su)
  
  mod_su_i <- fit_su_i$model
  
  
  # Growth ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_gr_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      state == "active",
      state_t1 == "active",
      size_t0 > 0,
      size_t1 > 0,
      is.finite(logsize_t0),
      is.finite(logsize_t1))
  
  fit_gr_i <- fit_poly_lm(
    df_gr_i, "logsize_t1", v_mod_set_gr)
  
  mod_gr_i <- fit_gr_i$model
  
  mod_gr_x_i <- fitted(mod_gr_i)
  mod_gr_y_i <- resid(mod_gr_i)^2
  
  mod_gr_var_i <- nls(
    mod_gr_y_i ~ a * exp(b * mod_gr_x_i),
    start = list(a = 1, b = 0),
    control = nls.control(
      maxiter = 1000, tol = 1e-6, warnOnly = TRUE))
  
  
  # Dormancy entry -------------------------------------------------------------
  df_do_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(enter_dormancy),
      size_t0 > 0,
      is.finite(logsize_t0))
  
  fit_do_i <- fit_poly_glm(
    df_do_i, "enter_dormancy", v_mod_set_do)
  
  mod_do_i <- fit_do_i$model
  
  
  # Reactivation ---------------------------------------------------------------
  df_ra_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(!is.na(reactivate))
  
  mod_ra_i <- glm(
    reactivate ~ 1,
    data = df_ra_i, family = "binomial")
  
  p_reactivate_i <- predict(
    mod_ra_i,
    newdata = data.frame(x = 1),
    type = "response")[1]
  
  df_ra_size_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      reactivate == 1,
      size_reactivate_t1 > 0) %>%
    mutate(
      logsize_reactivate = log(size_reactivate_t1))
  
  react_sz_i <- mean(
    df_ra_size_i$logsize_reactivate, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  react_sd_i <- sd(
    df_ra_size_i$logsize_reactivate, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  
  # Flowering ------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_fl_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      state == "active",
      !is.na(flower),
      size_t0 > 0,
      is.finite(logsize_t0))
  
  fit_fl_i <- fit_poly_glm(
    df_fl_i, "flower", v_mod_set_fl)
  
  mod_fl_i <- fit_fl_i$model
  
  
  # Flower number --------------------------------------------------------------
  df_fl_cond_i <- df_fl_i %>%
    filter(
      flower == 1,
      !is.na(fl_nr),
      fl_nr > 0,
      fl_nr %% 1 == 0)
  
  fit_fln_i <- fit_poly_nb(
    df_fl_cond_i, "fl_nr", v_mod_set_fl_n)
  
  mod_fln_i <- fit_fln_i$model
  
  
  # Recruitment ----------------------------------------------------------------
  df_sc2re_i <- df_re_i %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(nr_scapes),
      !is.na(recruits_simple)) %>%
    group_by(site, pop, year) %>%
    summarise(
      total_scapes = sum(nr_scapes),
      recruit_count = sum(recruits_simple), .groups = "drop")
  
  mods_re_i <- list(
    MASS::glm.nb(recruit_count ~ 1, data = df_sc2re_i),
    MASS::glm.nb(recruit_count ~ total_scapes, data = df_sc2re_i),
    MASS::glm.nb(
      recruit_count ~ log1p(total_scapes), data = df_sc2re_i))
  
  mod_re_i <- mods_re_i[[which.min(get_daicc(mods_re_i))]]
  
  df_sc2re_i <- df_sc2re_i %>%
    mutate(
      recruits_pred = predict(
        mod_re_i, type = "response"))
  
  recr_per_scape_i <- sum(df_sc2re_i$recruits_pred) /
    sum(df_sc2re_i$total_scapes)
  
  
  # Recruit size ---------------------------------------------------------------
  df_re_size_i <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      recruit_type == "seedling",
      size_t0 > 0,
      is.finite(logsize_t0))
  
  recr_sz_i <- mean(
    df_re_size_i$logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  recr_sd_i <- sd(
    df_re_size_i$logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  
  # IPM parameters -------------------------------------------------------------
  pars_i <- Filter(function(x) length(x) > 0, list(
    surv_b0 = get_coef(mod_su_i, "(Intercept)"),
    surv_b1 = get_coef(mod_su_i, "logsize_t0"),
    surv_b2 = get_coef(mod_su_i, "logsize_t0_2"),
    surv_b3 = get_coef(mod_su_i, "logsize_t0_3"),
    
    grow_b0 = get_coef(mod_gr_i, "(Intercept)"),
    grow_b1 = get_coef(mod_gr_i, "logsize_t0"),
    grow_b2 = get_coef(mod_gr_i, "logsize_t0_2"),
    grow_b3 = get_coef(mod_gr_i, "logsize_t0_3"),
    a = unname(coef(mod_gr_var_i)[["a"]]),
    b = unname(coef(mod_gr_var_i)[["b"]]),
    
    dorm_b0 = get_coef(mod_do_i, "(Intercept)"),
    dorm_b1 = get_coef(mod_do_i, "logsize_t0"),
    dorm_b2 = get_coef(mod_do_i, "logsize_t0_2"),
    dorm_b3 = get_coef(mod_do_i, "logsize_t0_3"),
    
    fl_b0 = get_coef(mod_fl_i, "(Intercept)"),
    fl_b1 = get_coef(mod_fl_i, "logsize_t0"),
    fl_b2 = get_coef(mod_fl_i, "logsize_t0_2"),
    fl_b3 = get_coef(mod_fl_i, "logsize_t0_3"),
    
    fln_b0 = get_coef(mod_fln_i, "(Intercept)"),
    fln_b1 = get_coef(mod_fln_i, "logsize_t0"),
    fln_b2 = get_coef(mod_fln_i, "logsize_t0_2"),
    fln_b3 = get_coef(mod_fln_i, "logsize_t0_3"),
    
    fecu_b0 = recr_per_scape_i,
    recr_sz = recr_sz_i,
    recr_sd = recr_sd_i,
    react_sz = react_sz_i,
    react_sd = react_sd_i,
    p_reactivate = p_reactivate_i,
    
    L = min(df_gr_i$logsize_t0),
    U = max(df_gr_i$logsize_t0),
    mat_siz = 200,
    
    mod_su_index = fit_su_i$index,
    mod_gr_index = fit_gr_i$index,
    mod_do_index = fit_do_i$index,
    mod_fl_index = fit_fl_i$index,
    mod_fl_n_index = fit_fln_i$index))
  
  lambda_ipm_i <- lambda_ipm(pars_i)
  
  
  # Observed population growth -------------------------------------------------
  last_complete_transition <- max_ind_year - dormancy_cutoff - 1
  
  df_counts_year_i <- df_counts_quad %>%
    filter(year <= last_complete_transition) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(
      n_quads = n(),
      n_t0 = sum(n),
      n_t1 = sum(n_t1), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_t0 > 0) %>%
    mutate(lambda_obs = n_t1 / n_t0)
  
  lambda_obs_arithmetic <- mean(
    df_counts_year_i$lambda_obs, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  lambda_obs_geometric <- exp(mean(
    log(df_counts_year_i$lambda_obs), na.rm = TRUE))
  
  
  # Scenario summary -----------------------------------------------------------
  n_absence_dead <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      state == "active",
      state_t1 %in% c("absent", "previous_absent"),
      survives == 0) %>%
    nrow()
  
  n_absence_unresolved <- df_ind_i %>%
    filter(
      state == "active",
      state_t1 %in% c("absent", "previous_absent"),
      is.na(survives)) %>%
    nrow()
  
  tibble(
    dormancy_cutoff = dormancy_cutoff,
    last_complete_transition = last_complete_transition,
    n_observed_transitions = nrow(df_counts_year_i),
    n_absence_dead = n_absence_dead,
    n_absence_unresolved = n_absence_unresolved,
    n_survival = nrow(df_su_i),
    n_survival_dead = sum(df_su_i$survives == 0),
    n_survival_alive = sum(df_su_i$survives == 1),
    survival_model_degree = fit_su_i$index,
    lambda_ipm = lambda_ipm_i,
    lambda_obs_arithmetic = lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    lambda_obs_geometric = lambda_obs_geometric)
}


# Run 0-20 years ----------------------------------------------------------------
df_sensitivity <- map_dfr(
  dormancy_cutoffs, run_dormancy_scenario)


# Summary relative to the current 3-year assumption ----------------------------
ref <- df_sensitivity %>%
  filter(dormancy_cutoff == reference_cutoff) %>%
  transmute(
    ref_ipm = lambda_ipm,
    ref_obs_arithmetic = lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    ref_obs_geometric = lambda_obs_geometric)

df_sensitivity_summary <- df_sensitivity %>%
  crossing(ref) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_ipm = lambda_ipm - ref_ipm,
    delta_obs_arithmetic =
      lambda_obs_arithmetic - ref_obs_arithmetic,
    delta_obs_geometric =
      lambda_obs_geometric - ref_obs_geometric,
    pct_delta_ipm = 100 * delta_ipm / ref_ipm,
    pct_delta_obs_arithmetic =
      100 * delta_obs_arithmetic / ref_obs_arithmetic,
    pct_delta_obs_geometric =
      100 * delta_obs_geometric / ref_obs_geometric) %>%
  select(-starts_with("ref_"))


# Final sensitivity plot -------------------------------------------------------
df_sensitivity_plot <- df_sensitivity_summary %>%
  select(
    dormancy_cutoff,
    `Mean IPM` = lambda_ipm,
    `Observed arithmetic` = lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    `Observed geometric` = lambda_obs_geometric) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -dormancy_cutoff,
    names_to = "estimate",
    values_to = "lambda")

fig_dormancy_sensitivity <- ggplot(
  df_sensitivity_plot,
  aes(
    x = dormancy_cutoff,
    y = lambda,
    linetype = estimate,
    shape = estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = reference_cutoff,
    linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = dormancy_cutoffs) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Sensitivity to terminal dormancy assumption",
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = "Maximum unresolved dormancy (years)",
    y = expression(lambda),
    linetype = NULL,
    shape = NULL)
```

The effect of the assumption on the number of classified deaths and unresolved
terminal absences, together with the resulting estimates of population growth,
is summarized below.

```{r dormancy-sensitivity-table, echo=FALSE}
df_sensitivity %>%
  select(
    dormancy_cutoff,
    n_absence_dead,
    n_absence_unresolved,
    n_survival_dead,
    lambda_ipm,
    lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    lambda_obs_geometric) %>%
  rename(
    `Dormancy cutoff (years)` = dormancy_cutoff,
    `Absences classified as dead` = n_absence_dead,
    `Unresolved absences` = n_absence_unresolved,
    `Deaths in survival model` = n_survival_dead,
    `Mean IPM lambda` = lambda_ipm,
    `Observed arithmetic lambda` = lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    `Observed geometric lambda` = lambda_obs_geometric) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The three-year reference assumption is indicated by the vertical dotted line.
The horizontal dashed line marks $\lambda = 1$, separating projected population
decline from population growth.

```{r dormancy-sensitivity-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
fig_dormancy_sensitivity
```


## Small individuals and extreme size reversals

Inspection of the diameter data identified a small number of unusually small
measurements among established plants. Small diameters are not inherently
problematic because genuine seedlings and young plants occur at these sizes.
The relevant concern is therefore restricted to active non-seedlings, especially
individuals showing an abrupt one-year reduction to a very small diameter
followed by a return to substantially larger size.

No diameter observations were corrected or removed. The following analyses are
used only to identify unusual observations and assess whether they can be
explained by other information in the demographic records.


```{r small-individuals-growth-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
# Annual growth transitions ----------------------------------------------------
df_growth_plot <- df_annual %>%
  arrange(id, year) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    state_t1 = lead(state_clean),
    stage_t1 = lead(stage_clean),
    dia_t1 = lead(dia)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_t1 == year + 1,
    state_clean == "active",
    state_t1 == "active",
    dia > 0,
    dia_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logdia_t0 = log(dia),
    logdia_t1 = log(dia_t1),
    flagged_small =
      (stage_clean != 1 & dia < 1) |
      (stage_t1 != 1 & dia_t1 < 1))


fig_small_growth <- ggplot(
  df_growth_plot,
  aes(
    x = logdia_t0,

  geom_abline(

    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = expression(log(Diameter[t])),
    y = expression(log(Diameter[t+1])))

fig_small_growth
```


```{r small-individuals-run, include=FALSE}
# Active non-seedlings below 1 cm ----------------------------------------------
df_annual <- df_annual %>%
  mutate(
    flag_low_nonseedling =
      state_clean == "active" &
      !is.na(stage_clean) &
      stage_clean != 1 &
      !is.na(dia) &
      dia < 1)


df_low_nonseedling <- df_annual %>%
  filter(flag_low_nonseedling) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    site, pop, qu, plant, id, year,
    stage_clean,
    dia, scape, invol, nb, nr, herb,
    comment) %>%
  arrange(year, site, pop, qu, plant)


# Three-year active histories --------------------------------------------------
df_three_year <- df_annual %>%
  arrange(id, year) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    year_prev = lag(year),
    year_next = lead(year),
    state_prev = lag(state_clean),
    state_next = lead(state_clean),
    dia_prev = lag(dia),
    dia_next = lead(dia),
    stage_prev = lag(stage_clean),
    stage_next = lead(stage_clean),
    scape_prev = lag(scape),
    scape_next = lead(scape),
    herb_prev = lag(herb),
    herb_next = lead(herb)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_prev == year - 1,
    year_next == year + 1,
    state_prev == "active",
    state_clean == "active",
    state_next == "active",
    dia_prev > 0,
    dia > 0,
    dia_next > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logdia_prev = log(dia_prev),
    logdia = log(dia),
    logdia_next = log(dia_next),
    valley_depth =
      pmin(logdia_prev, logdia_next) - logdia,
    local_valley =
      dia < dia_prev &
      dia < dia_next,
    strict_small_valley =
      dia < 1 &
      dia_prev >= 1 &
      dia_next >= 1)


# Strict large-small-large observations ---------------------------------------
df_suspicious <- df_three_year %>%
  filter(strict_small_valley) %>%
  arrange(desc(valley_depth))


df_suspicious_table <- df_suspicious %>%
  transmute(
    ID = id,
    Year = year,
    `Previous stage` = stage_prev,
    `Focal stage` = stage_clean,
    `Next stage` = stage_next,
    `Previous diameter` = dia_prev,
    `Focal diameter` = dia,
    `Next diameter` = dia_next,
    Scapes = scape,
    Herbivory = herb,
    `Valley depth` = valley_depth)


# Trajectories -----------------------------------------------------------------
df_suspicious_long <- df_suspicious %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, year,
    dia_prev, dia, dia_next) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(dia_prev, dia, dia_next),
    names_to = "position",
    values_to = "diameter") %>%
  mutate(
    census_year = case_when(
      position == "dia_prev" ~ year - 1,
      position == "dia" ~ year,
      position == "dia_next" ~ year + 1))


fig_suspicious_trajectories <- ggplot(
  df_suspicious_long,
  aes(
    x = census_year,
    y = diameter,
    group = id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Diameter")


# Flowering at small size ------------------------------------------------------
df_small_flowering <- df_annual %>%
  filter(
    state_clean == "active",
    !is.na(dia),

# Flowering and three-year size deviations ------------------------------------
df_fl_valley <- df_three_year %>%
  filter(!is.na(scape)) %>%
  mutate(
    flower = scape > 0,
    expected_dia =
      sqrt(dia_prev * dia_next),
    deviation_middle =
      log(dia / expected_dia))


df_flowering_valley_summary <- df_fl_valley %>%
  group_by(flower) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_deviation = mean(deviation_middle),
    median_deviation = median(deviation_middle),
    prop_local_valley = mean(local_valley),
    .groups = "drop")


# Herbivory check --------------------------------------------------------------
df_herb_test <- df_three_year %>%
  filter(herb %in% c(0, 1))


mod_herb_shrink <- lme4::lmer(
  log(dia) ~ log(dia_prev) + herb +
    (1 | year) +
    (1 | id),
  data = df_herb_test)


mod_herb_rebound <- lme4::lmer(
  log(dia_next) ~ log(dia) + herb +
    (1 | year) +
    (1 | id),
  data = df_herb_test)


herb_shrink_coef <-
  unname(lme4::fixef(mod_herb_shrink)[["herb"]])

herb_rebound_coef <-
  unname(lme4::fixef(mod_herb_rebound)[["herb"]])


# Summary ----------------------------------------------------------------------
df_small_summary <- tibble(
  Diagnostic = c(
    "Active non-seedling observations below 1 cm",
    "Strict >=1 -> <1 -> >=1 size reversals",
    "Flowering observations below 1 cm",
    "Flowering observations below 3 cm"),
  N = c(
    sum(df_annual$flag_low_nonseedling, na.rm = TRUE),
    nrow(df_suspicious),
    sum(
      df_annual$state_clean == "active" &
        !is.na(df_annual$dia) &
        df_annual$dia < 1 &
        !is.na(df_annual$scape) &
        df_annual$scape > 0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    nrow(df_small_flowering)))
```


There were only a small number of active non-seedling observations at extremely
small sizes. The most informative cases are those in which an established plant
was at least 1 cm in the preceding year, fell below 1 cm in the focal census,
and returned to at least 1 cm in the following year.

```{r small-individuals-summary, echo=FALSE}
df_small_summary %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


Seven observations met this strict definition. Their complete three-year size
sequences are shown below.

```{r small-individuals-table, echo=FALSE}
df_suspicious_table %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        `Previous diameter`,
        `Focal diameter`,
        `Next diameter`,
        `Valley depth`),
      ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r small-individuals-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
fig_suspicious_trajectories
```


The strongest reversals were substantially more extreme than ordinary annual
size variation. For example, the most pronounced sequence was 24.0, 0.5 and
19.9 cm in consecutive years. The focal observation was nevertheless recorded
as an active and flowering plant, with three scapes and recorded herbivory.
Other extreme reversals occurred without the same associated information, and
no common explanatory variable was identified across all seven observations.

## Flowering at very small size

Flowering at very small recorded diameter was itself rare.

```{r flowering-number-size-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5}

df_flowering_plot <- df_annual %>%

fig_flowering_number_size <- ggplot(

fig_flowering_number_size
```


```{r small-flowering-table, echo=FALSE}
df_small_flowering %>%
  rename(
    ID = id,
    Year = year,
    Stage = stage_clean,
    Diameter = dia,
    Scapes = scape,
    Herbivory = herb) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


The 0.5-cm observation was the only flowering record below 1 cm. However,
flowering itself does not appear to produce a general temporary reduction in
diameter. Across complete three-year histories, flowering observations had a
slightly positive rather than negative mean deviation from the size expected
from the preceding and following censuses.

```{r flowering-valley-summary, echo=FALSE}
df_flowering_valley_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Flowering = if_else(flower, "Yes", "No"),
    mean_deviation = round(mean_deviation, 3),
    median_deviation = round(median_deviation, 3),
    prop_local_valley = round(prop_local_valley, 3)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Flowering,
    N = n,

    `Median log deviation` = median_deviation,
    `Proportion local valleys` = prop_local_valley) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


Recorded herbivory may therefore provide a biologically relevant explanation
for the single most extreme observation, but it does not provide a general
explanation for the unusual size reversals. In the available observations with
herbivory coded as either absent or present, its estimated effects on size
reduction (`r round(herb_shrink_coef, 3)`) and subsequent recovery
(`r round(herb_rebound_coef, 3)`) were both small.

The unusual diameter records are therefore retained unchanged. Their primary
importance is that they represent a small set of potentially influential
observations that can later be examined explicitly in sensitivity analyses of
the growth model.



## Diameter measurement precision and heaping

A separate feature of the diameter data is the high frequency of exact integer
and half-unit measurements. This is distinct from the issue of unusually small
individuals. Here the question is whether particular numerical values indicate
isolated suspicious records or instead reflect the precision with which
diameter was recorded during different parts of the study.

```{r growth-heaping-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
# Growth plot with heaped diameter observations highlighted --------------------
df_growth_heap <- df_annual %>%
  arrange(id, year) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    state_t1 = lead(state_clean),
    dia_t1 = lead(dia)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_t1 == year + 1,
    state_clean == "active",
    state_t1 == "active",
    dia > 0,
    dia_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logdia_t0 = log(dia),
    logdia_t1 = log(dia_t1),

    integer_t0 = dia %% 1 == 0,
    integer_t1 = dia_t1 %% 1 == 0,

    half_t0 = (dia * 2) %% 1 == 0 & !integer_t0,
    half_t1 = (dia_t1 * 2) %% 1 == 0 & !integer_t1,

    heap_class = case_when(
      integer_t0 | integer_t1 ~ "Exact integer",
      half_t0 | half_t1 ~ "Half-unit only",
      TRUE ~ "Other"))


fig_growth_heaping <- ggplot(
  df_growth_heap,
  aes(
    x = logdia_t0,
    y = logdia_t1)) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(
    data = df_growth_heap %>%
      filter(heap_class == "Other"),
    alpha = 0.18,
    size = 1) +
  geom_point(
    data = df_growth_heap %>%
      filter(heap_class != "Other"),
    aes(color = heap_class),
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = expression(log(Diameter[t])),
    y = expression(log(Diameter[t+1])),
    shape = "Heaping")

fig_growth_heaping
```


```{r diameter-heaping-run, include=FALSE}

# Display summary --------------------------------------------------------------
df_heaping_display <- tibble(

# Figure -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  pivot_longer(
```
