

Across all positive active diameter observations, exact integer and half-unit
values were common.

```{r diameter-heaping-summary, echo=FALSE}
df_heaping_display %>%
  mutate(
    Proportion = round(Proportion, 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


However, this heaping was strongly structured through time.

```{r diameter-heaping-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
fig_heaping_year
```


In the earliest censuses almost all recorded diameters were integers. Integer
recording remained dominant through much of the 1990s, whereas from 2000 onward
the proportion of integer observations declined sharply and measurements at
finer decimal resolution became common. The same temporal pattern is evident
for measurements falling exactly on half-unit values.

This indicates that integer and half-unit values are primarily a feature of
changing measurement or recording resolution rather than a set of isolated
suspicious observations. In particular, there is no basis for treating values
such as exactly 1 or 2 cm as erroneous solely because they are integers.
Consequently, these observations are retained unchanged. The temporal change in
measurement precision should instead be kept in mind when interpreting the
growth data and its residual variation.



### Sensitivity of the growth model

The unusually small diameter observations may have disproportionate influence
on the growth model because a single extreme measurement contributes both a
large apparent shrinkage into the observation and a large apparent increase
from it in the following year. We therefore refitted the growth model under
three scenarios:

1. all observations retained;
2. transitions involving one of the seven strict
   `>= 1 -> < 1 -> >= 1 cm` reversals removed; and
3. transitions involving any active non-seedling diameter below 1 cm removed.

For a flagged diameter observation, both the transition entering and the
transition leaving that observation were excluded. No recorded diameter was
modified.


```{r growth-sensitivity-run, include=FALSE}
# Flag strict focal observations ----------------------------------------------
df_strict_key <- df_suspicious %>%
  dplyr::select(id, year) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(flag_strict_focal = TRUE)


# Growth data with endpoint flags ---------------------------------------------
df_growth_sensitivity <- df_annual %>%
  left_join(
    df_strict_key,
    by = c("id", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    flag_strict_focal =
      replace_na(flag_strict_focal, FALSE)) %>%
  arrange(id, year) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    state_t1 = lead(state_clean),
    dia_t1 = lead(dia),

    flag_low_t0 = flag_low_nonseedling,
    flag_low_t1 = lead(flag_low_nonseedling),

    flag_strict_t0 = flag_strict_focal,
    flag_strict_t1 = lead(flag_strict_focal)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_t1 == year + 1,
    state_clean == "active",
    state_t1 == "active",
    dia > 0,
    dia_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_t0 = log(dia),
    logsize_t1 = log(dia_t1),
    logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
    logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3,

    touches_strict =
      flag_strict_t0 |
      replace_na(flag_strict_t1, FALSE),

    touches_low_nonseedling =
      flag_low_t0 |
      replace_na(flag_low_t1, FALSE))


# Sensitivity datasets --------------------------------------------------------
growth_data_list <- list(
  `All observations` =
    df_growth_sensitivity,

  `Exclude strict reversals` =
    df_growth_sensitivity %>%
    filter(!touches_strict),

  `Exclude all <1 cm non-seedlings` =
    df_growth_sensitivity %>%
    filter(!touches_low_nonseedling))


# Same growth candidate models as the IPM -------------------------------------
growth_formulas <- list(
  logsize_t1 ~ 1,
  logsize_t1 ~ logsize_t0,
  logsize_t1 ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  logsize_t1 ~
    logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3)


fit_growth_scenario <- function(data, scenario) {

  mods <- lapply(
    growth_formulas,
    function(form) {
      lm(
        form,
        data = data)
    })

  aicc <- sapply(
    mods,
    function(mod) {
      k <- attr(logLik(mod), "df")
      n <- nobs(mod)

      AIC(mod) +
        2 * k * (k + 1) /
        (n - k - 1)
    })

  best_index <- which.min(aicc)
  mod <- mods[[best_index]]

  mod_gr_x <- fitted(mod)
  mod_gr_y <- resid(mod)^2

  mod_var <- nls(
    mod_gr_y ~ a * exp(b * mod_gr_x),
    start = list(
      a = 1,
      b = 0),
    control = nls.control(
      maxiter = 1000,
      tol = 1e-6,
      warnOnly = TRUE))

  list(
    scenario = scenario,
    data = data,
    model = mod,
    var_model = mod_var,
    degree = best_index - 1,
    aicc = aicc)
}


growth_fits <- imap(
  growth_data_list,
  ~ fit_growth_scenario(
    .x,
    .y))


# Model summary ---------------------------------------------------------------
get_growth_coef <- function(mod, term) {

  value <- coef(mod)[term]

  if (length(value) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  unname(value)
}


df_growth_sensitivity_summary <- map_dfr(
  growth_fits,
  function(x) {

    tibble(
      Scenario = x$scenario,
      N = nrow(x$data),
      `Excluded transitions` =
        nrow(df_growth_sensitivity) -
        nrow(x$data),
      `Selected degree` = x$degree,
      Intercept =
        get_growth_coef(
          x$model,
          "(Intercept)"),
      Linear =
        get_growth_coef(
          x$model,
          "logsize_t0"),
      Quadratic =
        get_growth_coef(
          x$model,
          "logsize_t0_2"),
      Cubic =
        get_growth_coef(
          x$model,
          "logsize_t0_3"),
      RMSE =
        sqrt(mean(resid(x$model)^2)),
      `Variance a` =
        unname(
          coef(x$var_model)[["a"]]),
      `Variance b` =
        unname(
          coef(x$var_model)[["b"]]))
  })


# Predicted growth curves -----------------------------------------------------
growth_grid <- tibble(
  logsize_t0 = seq(
    min(
      df_growth_sensitivity$logsize_t0),
    max(
      df_growth_sensitivity$logsize_t0),
    length.out = 300)) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
    logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3)


df_growth_predictions <- map_dfr(
  growth_fits,
  function(x) {

    growth_grid %>%
      mutate(
        Scenario = x$scenario,
        pred_logsize_t1 =
          predict(
            x$model,
            newdata = growth_grid))
  })


# Difference from the complete-data model -------------------------------------
df_growth_pred_wide <- df_growth_predictions %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Scenario,
    logsize_t0,
    pred_logsize_t1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Scenario,
    values_from = pred_logsize_t1)


df_growth_sensitivity_difference <-
  df_growth_pred_wide %>%
  summarise(
    `Strict reversals: max absolute difference` =
      max(
        abs(
          `Exclude strict reversals` -
            `All observations`)),
    `<1 cm non-seedlings: max absolute difference` =
      max(
        abs(
          `Exclude all <1 cm non-seedlings` -
            `All observations`))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "Comparison",
    values_to = "Max_difference")


# Growth sensitivity figure ---------------------------------------------------
fig_growth_sensitivity <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = df_growth_sensitivity,
    aes(
      x = logsize_t0,
      y = logsize_t1),
    alpha = 0.08,
    size = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(
    data = df_growth_predictions,
    aes(
      x = logsize_t0,
      y = pred_logsize_t1,
      linetype = Scenario),
    linewidth = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = expression(log(Diameter[t])),
    y = expression(log(Diameter[t+1])),
    linetype = NULL)
```


The sensitivity analysis changes only which observations are used to estimate
growth; all other demographic data remain unchanged.

```{r growth-sensitivity-table, echo=FALSE}
df_growth_sensitivity_summary %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        Intercept,
        Linear,
        Quadratic,
        Cubic,
        RMSE,
        `Variance a`,
        `Variance b`),
      ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r growth-sensitivity-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
fig_growth_sensitivity
```


In addition to changes in individual model coefficients, the fitted curves were
compared directly over the complete observed size range. The maximum absolute
difference in predicted log diameter after removing transitions involving the
seven strict reversals was
`r round(df_growth_sensitivity_difference$Max_difference[1], 4)`,
whereas removing transitions involving any of the active non-seedling
observations below 1 cm produced a maximum difference of
`r round(df_growth_sensitivity_difference$Max_difference[2], 4)` log-diameter
units.

Because the extreme observations can also affect the estimated spread of the
growth distribution, the table reports the parameters of the same
size-dependent residual-variance model used in the IPM. Thus, the sensitivity
analysis evaluates both the fitted mean growth relationship and the variance
around it rather than considering only changes in the regression line.




### Sensitivity to the treatment of new adults

The reconstruction of recruitment assumes that individuals first recorded as
new adults represent recruits that were missed during their seedling census.
The current analysis assigns these individuals to the recruitment cohort two
years before their first adult census. Although the size analysis supports this
interpretation particularly for stage-2 new adults, recruitment timing remains
inferred rather than observed.

We therefore compared five alternative treatments of new adults. All
non-recruit vital rates and the 3-year dormancy assumption were held constant,
so differences among scenarios isolate the effect of the recruitment
reconstruction.


```{r recruit-sensitivity-run, include=FALSE}
# Recruit classes --------------------------------------------------------------
df_recruit_first_sens <- df_recruit_first %>%
  mutate(
    recruit_class = case_when(
      recruit_type == "seedling" ~
        "observed_seedling",
      recruit_type == "new_adult" &
        stage == 2 ~
        "presumed_2yr",
      recruit_type == "new_adult" ~
        "new_adult_other"))


# Scenario names ---------------------------------------------------------------
recruit_scenarios <- c(
  "Current: all new adults = year-2 recruits",
  "Stage-2 only = year-2 recruits",
  "New adults enter only as adults",
  "All new adults = year-1 recruits",
  "Stage-2 only = year-1 recruits")


# Fixed reference demographic data --------------------------------------------
# Recruitment treatment does not alter survival, growth, dormancy, flowering
# or reactivation. These components are therefore fitted once at the reference
# 3-year dormancy cutoff.

df_recruit_reference <- make_scenario_data(
  reference_cutoff)

df_ind_recruit_reference <- df_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    row_type == "individual")


# Survival ---------------------------------------------------------------------
df_su_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    state == "active",
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0))

fit_su_rs <- fit_poly_glm(
  df_su_rs,
  "survives",
  v_mod_set_su)

mod_su_rs <- fit_su_rs$model


# Growth -----------------------------------------------------------------------
df_gr_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    state == "active",
    state_t1 == "active",
    size_t0 > 0,
    size_t1 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0),
    is.finite(logsize_t1))

fit_gr_rs <- fit_poly_lm(
  df_gr_rs,
  "logsize_t1",
  v_mod_set_gr)

mod_gr_rs <- fit_gr_rs$model

mod_gr_x_rs <- fitted(
  mod_gr_rs)

mod_gr_y_rs <- resid(
  mod_gr_rs)^2

mod_gr_var_rs <- nls(
  mod_gr_y_rs ~ a * exp(b * mod_gr_x_rs),
  start = list(
    a = 1,
    b = 0),
  control = nls.control(
    maxiter = 1000,
    tol = 1e-6,
    warnOnly = TRUE))


# Dormancy entry ---------------------------------------------------------------
df_do_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(enter_dormancy),
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0))

fit_do_rs <- fit_poly_glm(
  df_do_rs,
  "enter_dormancy",
  v_mod_set_do)

mod_do_rs <- fit_do_rs$model


# Reactivation -----------------------------------------------------------------
df_ra_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(reactivate))

mod_ra_rs <- glm(
  reactivate ~ 1,
  data = df_ra_rs,
  family = "binomial")

p_reactivate_rs <- predict(
  mod_ra_rs,
  newdata = data.frame(x = 1),
  type = "response")[1]


df_ra_size_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    reactivate == 1,
    size_reactivate_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_reactivate =
      log(size_reactivate_t1))

react_sz_rs <- mean(
  df_ra_size_rs$logsize_reactivate,
  na.rm = TRUE)

react_sd_rs <- sd(
  df_ra_size_rs$logsize_reactivate,
  na.rm = TRUE)


# Flowering --------------------------------------------------------------------
df_fl_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    state == "active",
    !is.na(flower),
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0))

fit_fl_rs <- fit_poly_glm(
  df_fl_rs,
  "flower",
  v_mod_set_fl)

mod_fl_rs <- fit_fl_rs$model


# Number of scapes -------------------------------------------------------------
df_fln_rs <- df_fl_rs %>%
  filter(
    flower == 1,
    !is.na(fl_nr),
    fl_nr > 0,
    fl_nr %% 1 == 0)

fit_fln_rs <- fit_poly_nb(
  df_fln_rs,
  "fl_nr",
  v_mod_set_fl_n)

mod_fln_rs <- fit_fln_rs$model


# Recruit size distribution ----------------------------------------------------
# This remains based on directly observed seedlings in every scenario.

df_re_size_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    recruit_type == "seedling",
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0))

recr_sz_rs <- mean(
  df_re_size_rs$logsize_t0,
  na.rm = TRUE)

recr_sd_rs <- sd(
  df_re_size_rs$logsize_t0,
  na.rm = TRUE)


# Base IPM parameters ----------------------------------------------------------
pars_recruit_base <- Filter(
  function(x) length(x) > 0,
  list(
    surv_b0 =
      get_coef(
        mod_su_rs,
        "(Intercept)"),
    surv_b1 =
      get_coef(
        mod_su_rs,
        "logsize_t0"),
    surv_b2 =
      get_coef(
        mod_su_rs,
        "logsize_t0_2"),
    surv_b3 =
      get_coef(
        mod_su_rs,
        "logsize_t0_3"),

    grow_b0 =
      get_coef(
        mod_gr_rs,
        "(Intercept)"),
    grow_b1 =
      get_coef(
        mod_gr_rs,
        "logsize_t0"),
    grow_b2 =
      get_coef(
        mod_gr_rs,
        "logsize_t0_2"),
    grow_b3 =
      get_coef(
        mod_gr_rs,
        "logsize_t0_3"),
    a =
      unname(
        coef(
          mod_gr_var_rs)[["a"]]),
    b =
      unname(
        coef(
          mod_gr_var_rs)[["b"]]),

    dorm_b0 =
      get_coef(
        mod_do_rs,
        "(Intercept)"),
    dorm_b1 =
      get_coef(
        mod_do_rs,
        "logsize_t0"),
    dorm_b2 =
      get_coef(
        mod_do_rs,
        "logsize_t0_2"),
    dorm_b3 =
      get_coef(
        mod_do_rs,
        "logsize_t0_3"),

    fl_b0 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fl_rs,
        "(Intercept)"),
    fl_b1 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fl_rs,
        "logsize_t0"),
    fl_b2 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fl_rs,
        "logsize_t0_2"),
    fl_b3 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fl_rs,
        "logsize_t0_3"),

    fln_b0 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fln_rs,
        "(Intercept)"),
    fln_b1 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fln_rs,
        "logsize_t0"),
    fln_b2 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fln_rs,
        "logsize_t0_2"),
    fln_b3 =
      get_coef(
        mod_fln_rs,
        "logsize_t0_3"),

    recr_sz = recr_sz_rs,
    recr_sd = recr_sd_rs,
    react_sz = react_sz_rs,
    react_sd = react_sd_rs,
    p_reactivate = p_reactivate_rs,

    L =
      min(
        df_gr_rs$logsize_t0),
    U =
      max(
        df_gr_rs$logsize_t0),
    mat_siz = 200,

    mod_su_index =
      fit_su_rs$index,
    mod_gr_index =
      fit_gr_rs$index,
    mod_do_index =
      fit_do_rs$index,
    mod_fl_index =
      fit_fl_rs$index,
    mod_fl_n_index =
      fit_fln_rs$index))


# Reference population counts -------------------------------------------------
df_counts_alive_rs <- df_ind_recruit_reference %>%
  filter(
    state %in%
      c(
        "active",
        "dormant",
        "alive_or_dormant")) %>%
  count(
    site, pop, qu, year,
    name = "n_alive")


last_complete_transition_rs <-
  max_ind_year -
  reference_cutoff -
  1


# One recruitment-treatment scenario -----------------------------------------
run_recruit_scenario <- function(scenario) {

  # Assign each observed entry to a recruitment cohort, or leave it as an
  # observed adult only.
  df_events_i <- df_recruit_first_sens %>%
    filter(
      !baseline) %>%
    mutate(
      fecundity_year = case_when(

        recruit_class ==
          "observed_seedling" ~
          recruit_year - 1,

        scenario ==
          "Current: all new adults = year-2 recruits" &
          recruit_type ==
          "new_adult" ~
          recruit_year - 2,

        scenario ==
          "Stage-2 only = year-2 recruits" &
          recruit_class ==
          "presumed_2yr" ~
          recruit_year - 2,

        scenario ==
          "All new adults = year-1 recruits" &
          recruit_type ==
          "new_adult" ~
          recruit_year - 1,

        scenario ==
          "Stage-2 only = year-1 recruits" &
          recruit_class ==
          "presumed_2yr" ~
          recruit_year - 1,

        TRUE ~ NA_real_),

      backfill_previous_year = case_when(

        scenario ==
          "Current: all new adults = year-2 recruits" &
          recruit_type ==
          "new_adult" ~
          TRUE,

        scenario ==
          "Stage-2 only = year-2 recruits" &
          recruit_class ==
          "presumed_2yr" ~
          TRUE,

        TRUE ~ FALSE))


  # Scenarios using year-2 reconstruction require monitoring through t + 2.
  requires_t2 <- scenario %in% c(
    "Current: all new adults = year-2 recruits",
    "Stage-2 only = year-2 recruits")


  # Count reconstructed recruits by fecundity year ----------------------------
  df_recruit_count_i <- df_events_i %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(fecundity_year)) %>%
    count(
      site,
      pop,
      qu,
      fecundity_year,
      name = "recruits")


  # Construct complete quadrat-year recruitment data --------------------------
  df_recruit_quad_i <- df_recruit_followup %>%
    mutate(
      recruitment_complete =
        monitored_t1 &
        if_else(
          requires_t2,
          monitored_t2,
          TRUE)) %>%
    filter(
      recruitment_complete) %>%
    left_join(
      df_recruit_count_i,
      by = c(
        "site",
        "pop",
        "qu",
        "year" =
          "fecundity_year")) %>%
    left_join(
      df_repro_quad %>%
        dplyr::select(
          site,
          pop,
          qu,
          year,
          nr_scapes),
      by = c(
        "site",
        "pop",
        "qu",
        "year")) %>%
    mutate(
      recruits =
        replace_na(
          recruits,
          0L))


  # Recruitment model ---------------------------------------------------------
  df_sc2re_i <- df_recruit_quad_i %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(nr_scapes)) %>%
    group_by(
      site,
      pop,
      year) %>%
    summarise(
      total_scapes =
        sum(nr_scapes),
      recruit_count =
        sum(recruits),
      .groups = "drop")


  mods_re_i <- list(
    MASS::glm.nb(
      recruit_count ~ 1,
      data = df_sc2re_i),

    MASS::glm.nb(
      recruit_count ~ total_scapes,
      data = df_sc2re_i),

    MASS::glm.nb(
      recruit_count ~
        log1p(total_scapes),
      data = df_sc2re_i))


  re_daicc_i <- get_daicc(
    mods_re_i)

  re_model_index_i <-
    which.min(
      re_daicc_i)

  mod_re_i <-
    mods_re_i[[
      re_model_index_i]]


  df_sc2re_i <- df_sc2re_i %>%
    mutate(
      recruits_pred =
        predict(
          mod_re_i,
          type = "response"))


  recr_per_scape_i <-
    sum(
      df_sc2re_i$recruits_pred) /
    sum(
      df_sc2re_i$total_scapes)


  # IPM lambda ----------------------------------------------------------------
  pars_i <-
    pars_recruit_base

  pars_i$fecu_b0 <-
    recr_per_scape_i

  lambda_ipm_i <-
    lambda_ipm(
      pars_i)


  # Scenario-specific observed population counts ------------------------------
  # Backfilling is used only when a new adult is assumed to have already been
  # present, but unobserved, in the preceding annual census.

  df_backfill_i <- df_events_i %>%
    filter(
      backfill_previous_year) %>%
    transmute(
      site,
      pop,
      qu,
      year =
        recruit_year - 1) %>%
    count(
      site,
      pop,
      qu,
      year,
      name =
        "n_backfill")


  df_counts_quad_i <- df_quad_monitor %>%
    left_join(
      df_counts_alive_rs,
      by = c(
        "site",
        "pop",
        "qu",
        "year")) %>%
    left_join(
      df_backfill_i,
      by = c(
        "site",
        "pop",
        "qu",
        "year")) %>%
    mutate(
      n_alive =
        replace_na(
          n_alive,
          0L),
      n_backfill =
        replace_na(
          n_backfill,
          0L),
      n =
        n_alive +
        n_backfill) %>%
    group_by(
      site,
      pop,
      qu) %>%
    arrange(
      year,
      .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      year_t1 =
        lead(year),
      n_t1 =
        lead(n),
      annual_transition =
        year_t1 ==
        year + 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(
      annual_transition,
      year <=
        last_complete_transition_rs)


  df_counts_year_i <- df_counts_quad_i %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(
      n_t0 =
        sum(n),
      n_t1 =
        sum(n_t1),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(
      n_t0 > 0) %>%
    mutate(
      lambda_obs =
        n_t1 / n_t0)


  lambda_obs_arithmetic_i <-
    mean(
      df_counts_year_i$lambda_obs,
      na.rm = TRUE)

  lambda_obs_geometric_i <-
    exp(
      mean(
        log(
          df_counts_year_i$lambda_obs),
        na.rm = TRUE))


  # Scenario summary ----------------------------------------------------------
  tibble(
    Scenario = scenario,

    `Recruit events used` =
      sum(
        !is.na(
          df_events_i$fecundity_year)),

    `Presumed 2yr used` =
      sum(
        df_events_i$recruit_class ==
          "presumed_2yr" &
          !is.na(
            df_events_i$fecundity_year)),

    `Other new adults used` =
      sum(
        df_events_i$recruit_class ==
          "new_adult_other" &
          !is.na(
            df_events_i$fecundity_year)),

    `Recruitment model` =
      re_model_index_i - 1,

    `Recruits per scape` =
      recr_per_scape_i,

    lambda_ipm =
      lambda_ipm_i,

    lambda_obs_arithmetic =
      lambda_obs_arithmetic_i,

    lambda_obs_geometric =
      lambda_obs_geometric_i)
}


# Run sensitivity --------------------------------------------------------------
df_recruit_sensitivity <- map_dfr(
  recruit_scenarios,
  run_recruit_scenario)


# Difference from current reconstruction --------------------------------------
ref_recruit <- df_recruit_sensitivity %>%
  filter(
    Scenario ==
      recruit_scenarios[1]) %>%
  transmute(
    ref_recr =
      `Recruits per scape`,
    ref_ipm =
      lambda_ipm,
    ref_obs_arithmetic =
      lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    ref_obs_geometric =
      lambda_obs_geometric)


df_recruit_sensitivity <- df_recruit_sensitivity %>%
  crossing(
    ref_recruit) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_recruits_per_scape =
      `Recruits per scape` -
      ref_recr,

    delta_ipm =
      lambda_ipm -
      ref_ipm,

    delta_obs_arithmetic =
      lambda_obs_arithmetic -
      ref_obs_arithmetic,

    delta_obs_geometric =
      lambda_obs_geometric -
      ref_obs_geometric) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    -starts_with("ref_"))


# Figure -----------------------------------------------------------------------
df_recruit_sensitivity_plot <- df_recruit_sensitivity %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Scenario,
    `Mean IPM` =
      lambda_ipm,
    `Observed arithmetic` =
      lambda_obs_arithmetic,
    `Observed geometric` =
      lambda_obs_geometric) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -Scenario,
    names_to = "Estimate",
    values_to = "lambda") %>%
  mutate(
    Scenario = factor(
      Scenario,
      levels =
        recruit_scenarios))


fig_recruit_sensitivity <- ggplot(
  df_recruit_sensitivity_plot,
  aes(
    x = Scenario,
    y = lambda,
    shape = Estimate)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.8,
    position =
      position_dodge(
        width = 0.4)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(lambda),
    shape = NULL) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x =
      element_text(
        angle = 25,
        hjust = 1))
```


The scenarios differ only in how first-record new adults contribute to
recruitment and whether their inferred presence is backfilled into the preceding
population census. Observed seedlings are treated identically in every
scenario, and all directly observed new adults remain in the demographic data.


```{r recruit-sensitivity-table, echo=FALSE}
df_recruit_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        `Recruits per scape`,
        lambda_ipm,
        lambda_obs_arithmetic,
        lambda_obs_geometric,
        delta_recruits_per_scape,
        delta_ipm,
        delta_obs_arithmetic,
        delta_obs_geometric),
      ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r recruit-sensitivity-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
fig_recruit_sensitivity
```


The comparison separates two uncertainties. Contrasting the current
reconstruction with the stage-2-only scenario tests whether the inference should
be restricted to the new adults whose stage and size are most consistent with
second-year recruits. The "new adults enter only as adults" scenario provides
the conservative alternative in which no new adult is used to infer recruitment
before its first observation. Finally, the year-1 scenarios test whether the
results depend specifically on assigning new adults to a two-year rather than a
one-year recruitment lag.
